summary: 2D screening label: not_2d_applicable. Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The input gate and scientific gate both failed, simulation_allowed is false, and comparison_valid is false. The selected scenario is Section 3.1 / Figure 4 of W2946670511: a two-tier flip-chip Mono3D IC versus a TSV-based 3D IC in HotSpot-6.0, 10 mm x 10 mm, with 400 um x 400 um hot spots at 750 W/cm2 and backgrounds of 25 and 30 W/cm2. The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady. That means a steady run with no transient trace, but no floorplan blocks or power_w rows were supplied, so the input validity check failed ("A custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object"). No bundled EV6/GCC adaptation and no pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace assets with a generated placement were used, so no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace exists, and there is no source commit or generated-placement assumption to report. No Studio temperatures exist, so nothing can be compared with the paper's approximate ~77 degC (Mono3D hot spots), ~109 degC (TSV-based upper-tier hot spots), ~38 degC tier difference in the TSV-based IC, or ~4 degC tier difference in the Mono3D IC. Even if a run were forced, the same location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions would not match, so only qualitative sensitivity could be discussed: vertical inter-tier coupling and TSV/interconnect heating are what drive the paper's tier-to-tier differences, and a 2D model cannot represent them. The verdict is gated by the feasibility decision and input validity, and it does not claim exact replication or numerical agreement with the paper.

3D stacked two-tier Mono3D and TSV-based structure (thin tiers, ILD or bonding layer, vertical inter-tier coupling and heat sink on top of the bottom tier). A 2D single-layer Studio model cannot reproduce vertical inter-tier heat flow, the upper-tier vs bottom-tier temperature difference, or TSV and MIV effects.

The paper models TSV arrays (4 arrays of 5 mm x 200 um x 33 um) and metal layers 1-8 with interconnect Joule heating (5% of tier power, 20% of which to TSVs). A 2D Studio model has no equivalent interconnect or TSV heating.

Hot spot coordinates for the four upper-tier hot spots and the per-block watts are not published, so no complete same-scenario floorplan and power set exists. Only dimensions (400 um x 400 um) and power densities are given (hot spot watts could be derived as density x area, but positions are missing).

The cooling configuration (heat sink and heat spreader parameters, convection resistance, ambient temperature) is not specified in the paper, and the paper's heat path runs through the bottom tier. A Studio package with a different cooling stack would give different temperatures.
The paper's solver is HotSpot-6.0 with multi-layer heterogeneous grids. The Studio solver and its grid and material treatment differ, so temperatures cannot be compared numerically.
The selected scenario is steady-state only, with no transient power trace, controller, optimizer or reliability analysis. A transient one-row trace would be purely illustrative.

Any Studio run would be a separate illustrative 2D placement built from the published dimensions (10 mm x 10 mm die, 400 um x 400 um hot spots) and power densities, with generated coordinates kept distinct from paper-derived facts.

Studio's bundled package and material assumptions (default silicon, TIM, heat spreader/sink, ambient and convection settings) are used instead of the paper's HotSpot-6.0 stack, whose parameters are not published.
Power would be a one-row constant (steady-state) trace.
Studio results would not be numerically compared with the paper's ~77 degC and ~109 degC values.
No exact replication of the paper is claimed.
